iterations.log: Fresh Opus subagent, skill only (no research notes). Scratch copy of game/ at /tmp/pilot/orbkin-render-look-1. S0 doctor ok; baseline audit + frozen captures (title, starter, desk + phone). Implemented: titleGrade tiltTop 3.6 @ 0.60 / tiltBottom 3.6 @ 0.36 / vignette 0.6; new starterGrade() 3.6 @ 0.66 / 3.6 @ 0.34 / vignette 0.5 (the starter shared meadowGrade with the meadow battle); Grade.tiltUnscaled for the low tier; title drift as a whole-internal-px setViewOffset shift with SpriteBaker.pan and a uPan dither lock; same-build switches post=oldscreens (byte-identical to the untouched build 4/4), drift=0, drift=truck. Results: check-budget PASS with every counter unchanged (fullResPasses 3 on phone, programs 64/63 unchanged); screen_metrics title-desk 0.34/0.97/0.31 top/focus/bottom; phones failed the skill's 640-px metric but passed at grid scale with the pilot's own diagnostic; focal crop diff non-zero on all four (vignette 0.4->0.6 reaches the trio, frame-90 pan raster); cam_analyze excess over idle: desk rigid 0.0067 / flick 0.0108 % / bad 0.043 %, phone 0.0124 / 0.0108 % / 0.066 % (old truck: 0.099 / 0.87 %); gate.py better 4/4 full frames with canary passed (crops: title-desk better, others no_difference); e2e hd2d-screens 6/6; SwiftShader benchFrames title +2.5..9.3 %, starter-desk +8.7..9.5 %, starter-phone +10.4..15.8 %. Bench cases proposed: title-low, starter-low, starter-low+oldscreens ablation.
skillProblems: doctor.sh had no --help (treated --help as the game dir and printed 'missing').

capture.mjs --repeat-check failed once on the untouched title-phone baseline (~1 % of pixels, a 1-internal-px drift shift) with no retry or guidance; root cause: the first game-loop dt depended on the fake clock's first rAF timestamp.
screen_metrics measured every view at 640 px wide: phone grids (271 px) read staircases as detail, so the outer-band <= 0.6 check could not pass on phones.
The focus-band orientation (Grade fractions are bottom-up, bands listed top-down) was undefined; the absolute 'focus >= 0.9' failed on content (starter-desk 0.85 before any change).

Defaults table claimed 'focal crop unchanged' for these numbers; the vignette step changes ~1 % of the subject crop by one level and a frozen frame at a non-zero pan rasterises differently after a camera change; no subject boxes were provided.

camera.md gave opposite dither signs in §2 and §3; the §3 recipe passed fullWidth/fullHeight as the sub-window, stored a 4-tuple, lacked the cam.view-disabled fallback and the pan reset in framed(), and reversed the old drift direction.
No mechanism for 'no low-tier tilt scaling on screens' and no warning that the starter grade is shared with the meadow battle.

No SwiftShader frame-time tool; the +10 % criterion sits inside the documented noise; cam_capture crashed when two ran concurrently; absolute S4 thresholds unreachable on a live screen (title idle floor rigid 0.32).
gate.py printed judge reasons into the generator's context while the gotchas said never to read judge vocabulary.

'passes = 3' ambiguous vs the audit's passes(all); npm run lint red on the untouched repo; no baseline-equivalence step for the same-build switch; the three bench cases were undefined for a screen change; the setup block referenced a missing bootstrap script and hard-coded /tmp paths.

judge.vsCurrent: Yes, it beats the current title and starter screens clearly on desk and modestly on phone: the symmetric 3.6 px bands plus the deeper vignette turn a flat, uniformly sharp meadow into a readable near/focus/far diorama with the trio and daises isolated and still pixel-crisp. It is a post-process gain only; it does not move the scene content closer to the reference bar, and the heavy bottom band plus 0.6 vignette trade away the dense pixel-flower foreground.
strengths: Depth hierarchy works: title-desk band profile 0.34 / 0.97 / 0.31 (top / focus / bottom); all four blind full-frame gates better in both orders with canary passed; sprites, daises and outlines byte-level crisp inside the focus band.

Blur quality is clean, not blocky or dithered: the 13-tap tilt inside the 640x360 grid with the nearest 2x upscale reads as a smooth lens blur; the image-locked Bayer dither does not crawl over blurred regions.
Phone portrait holds up: the trio and daises sit inside the sharp band, the DOM title/buttons and starter panel sit over blurred bands; grid-scale profiles 0.44/0.94/0.43 and 0.41/0.85/0.37.
The drift conversion is real and measured: excess rigid 0.0067 / flick 0.0108 % / rigid_bad 0.043 % on desk, 0.0124 / 0.0108 % / 0.066 % on phone, while the old truck fails (0.099 / 0.866 %).
Process evidence is coherent end to end: identical counters, byte-identical switch baseline, e2e 6/6, per-view gate JSONs, cam JSONs with excess, a candid 'still weak' list.
Good engineering judgement beyond the skill: separate starterGrade(), Grade.tiltUnscaled, drift=0/truck switches, a grid-scale diagnostic when the skill script could not pass phones.
weaknesses: Strength is on the heavy side for a title: the bottom 36 % becomes featureless green mush and the 0.6 vignette muddies the corners; the owner should see a lighter variant (2.4-3.0 px / 0.5 vignette) before this ships.
The 'focal crop unchanged' criterion failed on all four shots (vignette reaches the trio's edges, drift raster differs at frame 90, starter-phone focusBottom clips the dais bottoms).
SwiftShader frame time: starter-phone +10.4 % / +15.8 % against a +10 % criterion, with noise about +/-10 %; the phone cost is unknown until the real-phone bench runs.
The skill's phone sharpness metric could not pass; phone verdicts rest on the pilot's own diagnostic script.
Drift direction follows the old truck rather than camera.md's documented '+nx right'; the §3 sign-check capture was not run.
Phone crop gates were all no_difference and the title-phone crop leaned baseline, so there is no positive phone-crop evidence that blur quality near the silhouettes improved.
skillFixes: screen_metrics.py: downscale each capture to its internal grid (from the capture's .json meta) before the 12-band profile instead of hard-coding 640 px.
screen_metrics.py --focus-band: accept the Grade's bottom-up focusBottom,focusTop and convert internally; replace the absolute 'focus >= 0.9' with a delta against --before.
Defaults table: qualify 'focal crop unchanged'; state that a vignette change touches any subject wider than the centre third and that focal identity is measured with the camera held at pan 0.
Emit subject boxes from the stage into the capture meta and let screen_metrics --focal and gate.py --crop take 'subjects'.

camera.md: fix the dither sign contradiction, store the 6-tuple, pass v.width/v.height, add the cam.view-disabled fallback, reset the pan in framed(), state the drift direction, make the sign-check a required S4 step; publish the measured idle floors and write thresholds as excess over idle.
pipeline-api.md + Gotchas: add the tiltUnscaled mechanism and the shared starter grade warning; replace file:line references with grep anchors.
doctor.sh --help; capture.mjs retry a differing repeat once with a diff percentage and a documented policy; gate.py --quiet by default with reasons only in the JSON.
Add a frametime.mjs (interleaved A/B rounds via benchFrames, median and spread) or drop the +10 % SwiftShader criterion; serialise cam_capture runs.
S2: mandatory baseline-equivalence step (old switch cmp byte-identical with the S0 captures); lint line npx eslint src e2e; rename 'passes' to fullResPasses in summaries.

bench.md + bench.ts: define screen ablation cases and the decision rule for screen-grade changes; setup block: mark the missing bootstrap script and use an OUT variable instead of hard-coded /tmp paths; add an owner-taste step requiring a lighter candidate when a band or vignette is strengthened.
